chunks: And from him, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Fadalah, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both):

Regarding a man who says to his slave: 'I have freed you on the condition that I marry you to my female slave; if you marry her or take her as a concubine, then one hundred dinars are upon you.' He freed him on that basis, so he took her as a concubine and married her. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The condition is upon him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling when a slave is freed on the condition of marrying his master's female slave?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the principle of *al-shartu awla ma wafa'u bihi* (the condition is most worthy of fulfillment) within Shia jurisprudence, validating specific stipulations in manumission contracts. It highlights the scholarly consensus that a master may impose financial penalties or conditions upon a freed slave, provided they are explicitly agreed upon, thereby linking the legal status of the slave to contractual obligations rather than mere emancipation.
